Quick answer

Three versions, one goal.

All three are multivitamin and mineral sachets for daily use. They differ in registration, how complete the formula is, and how you take them.

LifePak® Indonesia

The version sold in Indonesia. It carries a BPOM number and an Indonesian label. One sachet holds 4 tablets: vitamins, minerals and phytonutrients (alpha-lipoic acid, polyphenols, carotenoids).

30 sachets · about 15 days · POM SI 054519191

Pick this if
  • You want one that is BPOM-registered with an Indonesian label
  • You want a full multivitamin and mineral without fish oil
  • You are not sure where to start, this is a reasonable starting point

LifePak® Nano+

The most complete version. 33 ingredients in one sachet, including fish oil (omega-3), CoQ10, alpha-lipoic acid and plant ingredients. The box I photographed is the Japan version.

60 sachets · about 30 days

Pick this if
  • You want the most complete formula in one sachet
  • You want omega-3 and CoQ10 included, without buying separate bottles
  • You do not mind several capsules and tablets per sachet

LifePak® Tablet

The compact base version. Core vitamins and minerals, plus olive fruit extract and grape seed extract. One sachet holds 4 small tablets and 1 softgel. The box I photographed is the Japan version.

30 sachets · about 15 days

Pick this if
  • You want a simple vitamin and mineral foundation
  • You want small pills and fewer ingredients
  • You want to try first before moving up to a fuller one

One box of Nano+ lasts about 30 days, while the Indonesian version and Tablet last about 15 days per box. So when you compare, count per month, not per box. For the monthly price, ask on WhatsApp. I will send you the numbers the same day.

Inside the sachet

What is actually in there.

One sachet of LifePak Indonesia

I opened one sachet and this is what is in it, four tablets. The box says each sachet consists of 1 vitamin tablet, 2 mineral tablets and 1 phytonutrient tablet. Two sachets a day, so 8 tablets in total. The batch number on the sachet matches the box.

One sachet of LifePak Tablet

I tore open one sachet and this is what is inside. Four small cream tablets and one red softgel. Two sachets a day, so eight tablets and two softgels in total. The box does not explain the red softgel separately.

How Nano+ is built

On the back of the box, Nu Skin Japan describes five methods it calls NNNDL. The idea is that it is not only which ingredients go in, but how they are chosen, combined and packed.

Nutrient FormsThe form and source of each ingredient is reviewed one by one.
Nutrient InteractionsIngredients are combined with attention to how they work together.
Nano TechnologyNano technology is used for fat-soluble ingredients that are hard to absorb.
Delivery FormatShape and size are made easy to take consistently.
LiponutrientsFat-soluble ingredients are made as softgels.

This is the explanation printed by Nu Skin on the pack. Results differ from person to person.

Why LifePak

What the boxes can actually back up.

01

One routine, not many bottles

The Indonesian version brings vitamins, minerals, alpha-lipoic acid, polyphenols and carotenoids together in 4 tablets per sachet. Nano+ gathers 33 ingredients, and Tablet vitamins, minerals and two plant extracts. Less to remember each day. If your diet is already very good and your doctor says you are not lacking anything, you may simply not need a supplement.

02

Clear origin and registration

The Indonesian box prints BPOM number POM SI 054519191, the manufacturer Capstone Nutrition (USA) and the importer PT Nu Skin Distribution Indonesia. The Nano+ box names a factory in Japan certified to supplement GMP (referencing pharmaceutical standards) and FSSC22000 for food safety.

03

Nano+ carries anti-doping certification

Nano+ carries the Informed Choice logo, a banned-substance testing programme for sport run by LGC in the UK. It screens for banned substances, it is not proof of effect. But it is useful if you train regularly and are careful about what is in your supplements.

What LifePak is not. Not a medicine, not a replacement for a balanced diet, and not a weight-loss programme. The boxes themselves point to a balanced diet as the base. If your goal is fat loss, LifePak is the nutrition foundation, and the programme is ageLOC® TRME® (page in Indonesian).

FAQ

Frequently asked.

Which one is officially sold in Indonesia?

The Indonesian version. Its box prints BPOM POM SI 054519191, has an Indonesian label, and is imported by PT Nu Skin Distribution Indonesia. The Nano+ and Tablet I photographed are Japan packaging with no BPOM number on the box. For whether they are available to you, ask me directly.

How many a day and when do I take them?

The Indonesian box says two sachets a day, each with 200 ml of water, after a main meal (for example breakfast and lunch, breakfast and dinner, or lunch and dinner). The Tablet box says about 2 sachets a day. Nu Skin material for Nano+ also says about 2 sachets a day. Follow the directions on the box you receive, and ask me if you are unsure.

Is it okay during pregnancy or nursing?

The Indonesian box says to avoid use during pregnancy or nursing. The Tablet box advises talking to a doctor or pharmacist first. I suggest the same for all three.

I take regular medication. Is it okay?

Ask your doctor or pharmacist first. The Indonesian box says to take care when combined with diabetes medication, and that supplements containing chromium are not advised for routine use. It also advises regular check-ins with a doctor. If you take blood thinners or have surgery coming up, be especially careful with Nano+ because it contains fish oil. Bring your medication list and the label photos from this page so they can assess.

Are there side effects?

The Indonesian box lists possible headache, dizziness and fatigue, and dark-coloured stool. If these appear and bother you, stop and ask a doctor.

I have a food allergy.

Check the ingredient lists above. Nano+ and Tablet contain gelatin, and Nano+ contains fish oil. The Indonesian version does not list gelatin in its other ingredients, but still check the label of the box you receive. If anything does not suit you, do not take it.

The colour of the pills looks uneven, is that okay?

The Tablet box explains that the surface colour can sometimes look darker in places because of the moisture in the softgel, and that this does not affect quality.

Why are Nano+ and Tablet labelled in Japanese?

The boxes I photographed are the Japan-market versions. I have translated the important parts on this page. If you need one with an Indonesian label and a BPOM number, that is the Indonesian version above.

Do I need fish oil separately?

Nano+ already lists pure fish oil among its ingredients. The Indonesian version and Tablet do not have fish oil as an active ingredient. Whether you need it depends on your situation, so ask me or your doctor.

Is it better to buy single vitamins?

It can be, if you know exactly what you lack and stay disciplined with the schedule. LifePak is for people who want one simple routine. If you have had blood tests, show the results to your doctor first.

What does it cost and where do I buy?

Prices and stock change, so ask directly on WhatsApp. Purchases go through official Nu Skin, and I help you from the start until you are comfortable with how to take it.

Still not sure which one?

Tell me about your eating habits and your goal. I will answer plainly. I am not a doctor, so for medical questions I send you to yours.
